\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{चूँकि} (cū̃ki)}{चूँकि (cū̃ki)}]{\hi{चूँकि} (cū̃ki) — since, as (giving a cause)}

\label{lesson:HI-C343-cuki}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for turning over (in bed), then the Hindi for a stretch (of the body).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{चूँकि}}
\textbf{\hi{चूँकि}} — \emph{cū̃ki} — \textquotedblleft{}since, as (giving a cause)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{चूँकि} \hi{बारिश} \hi{हो} \hi{रही} \hi{थी}, \hi{इसलिए} \hi{हम} \hi{घर} \hi{पर} \hi{रहे।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{cū̃ki bāriś ho rahī thī, isliye ham ghar par rahe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Since it was raining, we stayed at home.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{चूँकि}} (\emph{cū̃ki}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{chūnki}, \textquotedblleft{}since, because\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cū̃ki}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cū̃ki}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cū̃ki bāriś ho rahī thī, isliye ham ghar par rahe.} — Since it was raining, we stayed at home.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for turning over (in bed), then the Hindi for a stretch (of the body), then say \emph{cū̃ki} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{चूँकि} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Since, as (giving a cause)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{असर} (asar)}{असर (asar)}]{\hi{असर} (asar) — an effect}

\label{lesson:HI-C343-asar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a stretch (of the body), then the Hindi for since.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{असर}}
\textbf{\hi{असर}} — \emph{asar} — \textquotedblleft{}an effect\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{दवा} \hi{का} \hi{असर} \hi{दो} \hi{घंटे} \hi{बाद} \hi{हुआ।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{davā kā asar do ghaṇṭe bād huā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The medicine took effect two hours later.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{असर}} (\emph{asar}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{athar}, \textquotedblleft{}a trace, a mark\textquotedblright{}, which reached Hindi through Persian. Hindi uses it for the effect one thing has on another.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{asar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{asar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{davā kā asar do ghaṇṭe bād huā.} — The medicine took effect two hours later.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a stretch (of the body), then the Hindi for since, then say \emph{asar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{असर} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An effect\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{जुड़ना} (juṛnā)}{जुड़ना (juṛnā)}]{\hi{जुड़ना} (juṛnā) — to be joined, to be linked}

\label{lesson:HI-C343-jurna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for since, then the Hindi for an effect.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{जुड़ना}}
\textbf{\hi{जुड़ना}} — \emph{juṛnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to be joined, to be linked\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{पेड़} \hi{की} \hi{हर} \hi{डाली} \hi{उसकी} \hi{जड़} \hi{से} \hi{जुड़ती} \hi{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{peṛ kī har ḍālī uskī jaṛ se juṛtī hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Every branch of a tree is joined to its root.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \hi{वह} \hi{पुल} \hi{सड़क} \hi{से} \hi{जुड़} \hi{गया}, \emph{vah pul saṛak se juṛ gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{जुड़ना}} (\emph{juṛnā}) is inherited from \emph{*yuṭati}, \textquotedblleft{}joins\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs from its descendants (CDIAL 10496).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{juṛnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{peṛ kī har ḍālī uskī jaṛ se juṛtī hai.} — Every branch of a tree is joined to its root.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for since, then the Hindi for an effect, then say \emph{juṛnā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{आधार} (ādhār)}{आधार (ādhār)}]{\hi{आधार} (ādhār) — a basis, grounds}

\label{lesson:HI-C343-adhar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for an effect, then the Hindi for to be joined.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{आधार}}
\textbf{\hi{आधार}} — \emph{ādhār} — \textquotedblleft{}a basis, grounds\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{तुम्हारी} \hi{बात} \hi{का} \hi{आधार} \hi{क्या} \hi{है}?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tumhārī bāt kā ādhār kyā hai?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
What are your grounds for saying that?
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{आधार}} (\emph{ādhār}) is a tatsama, borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{ādhāra}, \textquotedblleft{}a support, a prop\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ādhār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ādhār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tumhārī bāt kā ādhār kyā hai?} — What are your grounds for saying that?
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for an effect, then the Hindi for to be joined, then say \emph{ādhār} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{ज़िम्मेदार} (zimmedār)}{ज़िम्मेदार (zimmedār)}]{\hi{ज़िम्मेदार} (zimmedār) — responsible}

\label{lesson:HI-C343-zimmedar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for to be joined, then the Hindi for a basis, grounds.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{ज़िम्मेदार}}
\textbf{\hi{ज़िम्मेदार}} — \emph{zimmedār} — \textquotedblleft{}responsible\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{दुर्घटना} \hi{के} \hi{लिए} \hi{ड्राइवर} \hi{ज़िम्मेदार} \hi{था।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{durghaṭnā ke liye ḍrāivar zimmedār thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The driver was responsible for the accident.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{ज़िम्मेदार}} (\emph{zimmedār}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{zimmadār}, \textquotedblleft{}answerable, in charge\textquotedblright{}. The ending \emph{-dār} is the Persian \textquotedblleft{}holding\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{zimmedār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{durghaṭnā ke liye ḍrāivar zimmedār thā.} — The driver was responsible for the accident.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for to be joined, then the Hindi for a basis, grounds, then say \emph{zimmedār} again
\end{itemize}
